title: Clauses, guards and functions as values
hints: A guard goes after the arguments: def sign(n) when n > 0, do: :positive
Put the fizzbuzz clause for 15 first. The first matching clause wins.
apply_n: one clause for n of 0 that returns the value, and one that calls apply_n(fun, n - 1, fun.(value)).
compose returns fn x -> g.(f.(x)) end. Remember the dot when calling a function held in a variable.
